title: Seasonal slopes raised six-month PDO forecast error by 2.54% in a 1981-2025 test
abstract: We tested annual changes in PDO and Nino 3.4 slopes in direct six-month PDO forecasts. We used fixed NOAA ERSSTv5 snapshots and 540 targets in 1981-2025. Each fit used earlier completed targets only. Four annual interaction terms raised mean squared error from 1.050266 to 1.076907 PDO index squared, an increase of 2.54%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval for the increase was 1.07% to 3.85%. Three- and seven-year blocks also indicated higher error. A 30-year fit gave a 3.28% increase. One- and twelve-month tests had intervals across zero. This test favors common slopes over this seasonal model at six months. It does not show that physical ocean memory or tropical forcing lacks seasonal change. Revised shared-source indices, simple models, dependent years and uncertainty conditional on fitted predictions limit inference. Code, provenance, aggregate evidence, a figure and an independent numerical audit are included. External raw data and monthly records are regenerated outside the publication.

display.caption: Seasonal slopes increased six-month forecast error in the stated 1981-2025 test. Intervals are conditional paired five-year block intervals.

citations.reason: Public reference model, dates and sources informed this extension. Shared data; not independent confirmation.
